summary: This review surveys tantalum as a superconducting thin-film material for quantum circuits, covering growth mechanisms, phase selection on various substrates, fabrication techniques, and performance in resonators and qubits. Key unresolved issues include the role of $\eta$-phase impurities, HF effects on circuit characteristics, and anomalous low-temperature behavior of $\alpha$-tantalum.
motivation: Tantalum has recently demonstrated breakthrough coherence performance in superconducting microwave resonators and qubits compared to conventional aluminum and niobium, motivating systematic study of its material properties and fabrication.
method: The authors review recent work on tantalum thin-film growth, crystalline phase selection mechanisms across different substrates, superconducting circuit fabrication and performance, and first-principles theoretical modeling of the material.
result: Tantalum exhibits distinctive cryogenic behavior not observed in aluminum or niobium circuits, but several open questions remain about $\eta$-phase impurity effects, HF-induced degradation mechanisms, and the nature of $\alpha$-tantalum anomalies at low temperatures.
